sections.h2: Where a Barren County deed gets recorded
sections.html:
The Barren County Clerk's office sits in the Barren County Government Center on the north side of the square, at 117 North Public Square, Suite 1A, Glasgow, KY 42141. The phone number is 270-651-3783. Every deed and mortgage on Barren County land is recorded there.

Under KRS 382.110 the filing belongs to the county that contains the land. A house in Cave City, Park City, Glasgow or near Barren River Lake is recorded in Glasgow, wherever the seller lives now. The same Legal Records Division collects delinquent real estate taxes, so back taxes on a house come up at this counter as well.

sections.h2: What else the clerk's office handles
sections.html:
Besides land records, the Glasgow office issues marriage licenses, notary commissions and going-out-of-business licenses. Its Motor Vehicle Division registers or renews more than 40,000 vehicles a year, collects county vehicle taxes including motorboats, issues decals, plates and disabled parking permits, and files liens on titled collateral. The Legal Records Division records and indexes every real estate document, among them powers of attorney, assignments, releases and UCC fixture filings.

One trip can cover several errands. A closing agent can bring the deed and a release in the same visit.

sections.h2: How much it costs to record a deed
sections.html:
The posted schedule took effect January 1, 2020, and the office points to KRS 64.012 and House Bill 537 as its basis. Pages beyond the fifth cost $3 each on most filings, while a mortgage waits until page thirty-one for that surcharge.

Minimum recording fees at the Barren County Clerk
FilingMinimum fee
Deed or condominium deed$50
Easement$50
Real estate lease$50
Option agreement, real estate$50
Mortgage with assignment$126
Judgment lien$46
Lis pendens notice$46
Mechanic lien release$46

KRS 142.010 separately puts a $4 state tax on a real property conveyance, which the clerk collects. Request one all-in figure at the counter.

The clerk's recording page lists the usual reasons a filing comes back. Nearly all can be prevented, and a returned deed can push a closing back.

  • The document is not notarized, or the notary left off an expiration date or the date of notarization.
  • The filing fee is wrong or the check is unsigned.
  • The title source is incomplete, or there is no legal description of the property.
  • No in-care-of address appears for the tax bill.
  • The grantor or grantee mailing address is missing.
  • A copy was submitted where an original is required.
  • A power of attorney lacks two disinterested witnesses, a rule the clerk ties to KRS 457.050 effective July 15, 2018.

The in-care-of address and full-consideration requirements come from KRS 382.135, and the title source rule comes from KRS 382.110. Attorneys catch these routinely. If you drafted the deed yourself, go down the list line by line.

The seller owes fifty cents for each $500 of value in the deed, and any leftover part of $500 is rounded up (KRS 142.050). The clerk figures the amount and holds the deed until it is paid.

The tax is paid at the counter when the deed is filed, so the closing agent normally deducts it from the seller's proceeds and brings the payment along with the fees. If the deed recites a price that looks unusually low for a sale between strangers, expect questions, since the tax is figured on the value stated.

No tax applies to a deed that only corrects an earlier deed, ties or frees a debt, follows a foreclosure, or passes between spouses, nor to a parent-child transfer for token consideration. For a gift, the base is market value.

After the sheriff's collection season closes, an unpaid bill becomes the clerk's concern, since the Legal Records Division collects delinquent real estate taxes. April 15 is the cutoff. The clerk then holds a certificate of delinquency, a lien goes on record, interest of 1 percent monthly begins, and fees for the county attorney and clerk follow.

KRS 134.015 sets December 31 as the due date, a 2 percent discount through November 1 and a 5 percent penalty in January. Because the balance grows monthly, get the clerk's payoff figure close to the closing date.

Online land records come through eCCLIX, sold by Software Management, LLC. A monthly account costs $200 to start, $65 monthly and $10 per extra user. A one-day account costs $45 to start and $15 for each 24 hours. Viewing at the clerk's office costs nothing.

DocAlert is a free email notice from the same vendor. It fires when a mortgage or deed is filed under a registered personal or business name. Landlords with several parcels, and heirs who live far away, can use it to spot a forged filing.

If you only need to look something up, such as the book and page of your own deed, free walk-in viewing is the cheapest route. Paid online access makes more sense for someone who searches often.

Closing agents who prefer not to visit the square can file electronically through CSC, Simplifile or ePN. Contact details for each vendor are on the clerk's recording page.

Barren County covers roughly 500 square miles of south-central Kentucky, and Glasgow is its largest city. The estimated 2025 population is 45,641, which is 2.6 percent above the April 2020 base. Half of owner-occupied houses are worth more than $178,000, and owners live in 65.2 percent of 18,017 households. There were 20,957 housing units as of July 2025. Middle household income is $50,628 and middle gross rent is $796.

Agriculture is the main industry, Glasgow is the manufacturing, medical and retail center, and Cave City lives on visitors to Mammoth Cave. Paperwork differs by parcel type. A farm may involve several tracts and an older plat, and a lodging lot near Cave City may carry easements. Each such document is recorded at the clerk at prices like those in the fee table. Three school systems cover the county, so buyers often ask which one serves a particular house.

• Locate the book and page of the deed you hold.
  • Check with the clerk for a recorded delinquency certificate or lien.
  • Get the address where the buyer wants the next tax bill sent.
  • Agree on who files the deed, electronically or in person in Glasgow.
  • For an inherited parcel, ask whether an affidavit of descent is needed. The clerk lists it at $50.

Owners of a vacant or inherited Barren County house who prefer not to repair it can request a cash offer. Recording works the same way once a price is agreed.

faqs.q: Where is the Barren County Clerk's office?
faqs.a: Inside the Barren County Government Center at 117 North Public Square, Suite 1A, Glasgow. The phone number is 270-651-3783.

faqs.q: How much is the minimum fee to record a deed in Barren County?
faqs.a: A deed's minimum is $50, plus $3 for every page beyond five. The $4 state tax on conveyances in KRS 142.010 may apply on top, so ask for a full total.

faqs.q: Does Barren County accept electronic recording?
faqs.a: Yes. CSC, Simplifile and ePN are the e-recording services, so a title company can file without bringing paper to Glasgow.

faqs.q: What happens if my deed has no tax-bill address?
faqs.a: The clerk may return it. KRS 382.135 calls for an in-care-of address for that year's bill, and a missing address is on the clerk's rejection list.

faqs.q: Is there a way to be warned about a fake deed on my land?
faqs.a: Yes, DocAlert. Sign up on the clerk's website with a name and an email address, and a message goes out whenever a deed or mortgage is recorded under that name.
